purpose:
How far a character LoRA holds. One woman, one room, one light, one standing pose: the ONLY thing that changes between cells is how much of the frame she occupies, so the distance at which identity stops binding is measured rather than felt. The legend carries the two models that can load a character LoRA at all (Krea 2 Turbo and BigLust v1.6), so the same ladder reads on both. Prompts name no character - the trigger token and the LoRA supply the identity - so this catalog is reusable for the next character trained.

THE SCALE, MEASURED ON THE FIRST RUN (2026-10-04, Krea 2 Turbo with a character LoRA at 0.8) - read this before editing a rung. The operator's own 'far' reference is a face about 60 px across on a full standing figure with a whole scene around it; these far rungs returned a face about 130 px, a full figure FILLING the frame, so they were not far at all. The low end was wrong too: the close rung rendered slightly closer than intended and cut the top of her head off, leaving no face to judge. WHY: every far rung asked for distance as a demand about the person - 'the whole room in the frame with her standing small in it'. That is the same class of instruction the baseline dialect notes already record as never working on this family, and it did nothing here either; the render fell back to a normal framing. The distance in the operator's reference came from the SCENE - a large space, a landmark, and a camera placed across it. SO: distance is now stated as a fact about the SPACE and the camera's place in it - a long bare room, a window at the far end, an open doorway at the near end, and 'the whole length of the bare floor between the camera and her'. Nothing asks the figure to be small. This is a hypothesis until the next run; the near and medium rungs are unaffected, because a shot-size statement at that range does work.

TWO REQUIREMENTS THE FIRST RUN EXPOSED, both now met by every rung that should face the lens:
* FACING THE CAMERA IS STATED. Without it the model picks the pose, and it picks away from the lens about as often as toward it - which is worst exactly where it matters most, because at distance the face is the only thing carrying identity. The Krea 2 dialect forbids a face-facing clause FOR ACTS (it pulls the faces together and fights the act); there is no act here, so stating it is correct.
* EACH PERSON'S ORIENTATION IS NAMED in the group rungs, rather than left to a single clause covering three subjects.

Expected result, so it is not mistaken for a bug: identity is strong in the close cells and weakens as the figure shrinks, because a LoRA's grip scales with the pixels on the face - and on a model that declares no reference conditioning there is no second identity channel to recover it with. Two things vary the outcome and are worth running: canvas size (a far frame at 1536x1536 gives the face roughly twice the pixels of the same frame at 1024) and LoRA strength (the picker offers 0.6 to 1.0; 0.8 was the strength used in the 2026-10-03 runs). Only the declared SEED is applied by the render driver - steps, cfg, sampler and size come from the selected model's own qualified envelope, not from these files.
